subject: FluxLabs - concurrency decomposition & dedicated fleet sizing
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika@fluxlabs.ai>

Cc: Leo Martinez <leo@fluxlabs.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing starter & traffic snapshot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking time last week. As discussed, we're planning to move from bursty hosted endpoints to a reserved GPU pool for predictable latency and to reduce per-token cost. Sending a quick snapshot of this quarter's traffic (attached) and a short set of questions to help size the first dedicated cluster.

Quick context: production user-facing chat assistant, average session ~3 prompts (mostly short prompts, 40-120 tokens) + 1 follow-up generation ~150-400 tokens. Peak daily active users ~18k with peaks concentrated 09:00-12:00 PT. We expect 30% growth over next 6 months.

Questions we need answers to for internal ops planning:
- What concurrency per GPU should we assume for a Llama2-13B quantized variant?
- Recommended oversubscription guardrails for web chat workloads with small prompt + moderate response length (150-400 tokens)
- Latency SLO targets we can expect given 8xA100-style machines vs 4xH100 setups

Attaching fluxlabs_traffic_snapshot.csv that includes per-minute request counts for the last 14 days and a sample of prompt/response token distributions.

Can you share the sizing template you prefer? Also let's schedule a 30-minute technical review this week if possible — Leo and I are flexible after 10:30 PT.

Thanks,
Anika
Anika Rao
Head of Platform
FluxLabs

Hi Anika — thanks for the snapshot and the clear bullets. I reviewed the CSV quickly; nice granularity. I've attached our standard sizing workbook (redwood_sizing_template_v2.xlsx) that walks through the same inputs we use to produce a cluster footprint and OPEX estimate.

I copied Vivek (pre-sales lead) and Dev (inference infra) to help with the kernel/quantization and GPU-concurrency assumptions. Before we model, a few additional askables that will materially change recommendations:
- Typical prompt mix by feature (one-off prompts vs multi-step chat flows). If you have the telemetry tag breakdown, paste 3-5 example percentiles.
- Manifest for heavy multimodal requests (images/embeddings) if any — even at <5% they change GPU choices.
- Desired worst-case P99 generation latency (e.g., 300ms, 750ms, 1.5s).

Next steps: we'll take the CSV + your answers and run two scenarios: (A) cost-optimized reserved fleet (higher oversubscription, more batching), (B) SLO-first fleet (lower oversubscription, dedicated concurrency). Outcome will include GPU mix suggestions (H100 vs A100/RTX options), expected token cost delta, and an initial canary rollout plan.

I've penciled a 30-min review: Thu 2026-09-03 11:00 PT. Does that work?

Best,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing starter & traffic snapshot

Adding a few quick engineering heuristics to set expectations before we run the workbook:

- For a quantized Llama2-13B (8-bit or 4-bit QAT-like variants) with Redwood inference runtime optimizations, conservative concurrency assumptions per H100 (80GB) GPU for chat-style workloads are: 6-10 concurrent generation sessions if you target P95 <400ms for median prompt sizes (<=120 tokens) and response ~300 tokens.
- If you want P99 <750ms, plan for 3-5 concurrent sessions per GPU (depending on KV cache hits and batchability).
- Oversubscription: safe default is 1.25x for web chat; aggressive cost-first can go to 2.0x if latency SLOs are relaxed and prefix caching is high.
- Batching improves token throughput but increases tail latency; for user-facing chat we bias small batch windows (5-10ms) and smarter routing to preserve P99.

Dev — can you take the CSV and run a quick rollup that highlights: peak qps window (per-minute), median prompt tokens, median response tokens, and percent of sessions with multi-prompt >3? That will let us populate the sizing template.

Anika — Thu 11:00 PT works for me.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing starter & traffic snapshot

Attachments: fluxlabs_traffic_rollup_20260902.csv (csv, 450KB)

Hi all — I processed the CSV and dropped a concise rollup (attached). Highlights:
- Observed peak 1-minute QPS in the window: 1,130 req/min (~18.8 req/s) occurring on 2026-08-26 10:42 PT.
- Median prompt tokens: 65, median response tokens: 210.
- 19% of sessions have >3 prompts.
- Multi-modal calls (image embedding) are ~2.8% of requests and typically short responses.

Plugging these numbers into the redwood_sizing_template_v2.xlsx with our conservative concurrency (6 concurrent per H100) gives baseline fleet: 6xH100 GPUs for initial steady-state to hit P95 <400ms with a 1.25x oversubscription buffer. Cost-optimized variant (2.0x oversub) drops to 4xH100 equivalent but would increase P99 tail by ~30-60% depending on runtime caching.

I've also added a short sensitivity table in the sheet showing how growth and token-length shifts change the required GPU count.

Anika — please confirm whether FluxLabs wants the initial deployment to prioritize cost or latency; we'll finalize numbers in the Thu call and produce a short runbook for canary traffic splitting.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

We will be on the Thu call (confirmed) and will upload a small telemetry tag dump (per-feature percentiles) to the Drive link before the meeting. Also requesting that Redwood include a short section in the runbook on rollback triggers (token-cost spike thresholds, CPU/GPU temperature alerts, and queue-depth limits).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — see you Thursday 11:00 PT.

Best,
Anika
